messages:
maria_support: Forwarding a customer escalation from Juno Corp — they report that after our v7.1 model rollout responses feel "clipped" and less explanatory. Customer says this started ~2 hours after the deploy and affects their support-scripting flow. They're asking for a timeline and an immediate mitigation.

maria_support: Key quote from customer: 'answers used to provide 3-4 suggested follow-ups and a one-paragraph rationale; now it's one short directive with no context.' :frowning:

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: rwd-std-v7.1 rolled to hosted shard us-east-1 at 1819989000. Canary traffic 10% -> 100% at 1819991200.

akshay_engineer: thanks for flagging — can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + observed response) and the model name the customer called? also which decode params (temp/top_p) they used if known.

maria_support: Repro below from customer (copied verbatim). They call model rwd-std-v7.1 via our completions endpoint with default params (temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95).

maria_support: ```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
{
  "model": "rwd-std-v7.1",
  "prompt": "Customer: My payment failed during checkout. What should I do?\nAssistant:",
  "max_tokens": 200,
  "temperature": 0.2
}
```

maria_support: Customer's observed response (v7.1):

"Check your card and retry. If it still fails, contact support."

maria_support: Customer provided an archived example from last week (pre-rollout, v6.9) for the same prompt: 

"I'm sorry you hit a payment failure — please try the transaction again and verify your card details (expiry/CVV). If the problem persists, check with your bank for holds or limits; collect the error code from the payment provider and send it to support. We can also attempt a manual retry on our end. Would you like steps to retry or to open a support ticket?"

maria_support: Customer metrics: average token count per response dropped ~45% in their logs. They flagged missing hedging language and fewer suggested actions.

devon_research: this reads like a formatting/verbosity regression rather than hallucination or safety. @akshay_engineer can you run a quick A/B with rwd-std-v6.9 vs v7.1 on a small prompt set (n=50) and compute average token length + number of suggestion clauses (heuristic: sentences containing '?', 'Would you', 'You can'). I can script the eval if you want.

akshay_engineer: on it. do we have the customer's prompt set or should I seed with a support-focused prompt bank? also, any chance the serving defaults changed (e.g., logits temperature, repetition_penalty) during rollout?

maria_support: I have a small set of 12 prompts from the customer — attaching inline below. use them verbatim: 
1) "My payment failed during checkout. What should I do?"
2) "App crashes when I upload a file, any pointers?"
3) "How do I reset a forgotten 2FA device?"

maria_support: Their team confirmed they didn't change client-side params. They hit the hosted API with our SDK default config.

akshay_engineer: quick logs from our side show no decode-param override in the rollout manifest, but there's a new post-filter step in the v7.1 serving path that trims trailing sentences over 140 chars if latency spike detected. tagging @ops_oncall — could that autopruning be too aggressive?

ops_oncall: I see the autoscaling trigger fired for us-east-1 around 1819991000 and the flakiness cutover engaged the latency guardrails. If the post-filter was enabled as a safety measure it might be truncating helpful context. I'll temporarily disable the post-filter for the affected shard and keep it off while we validate.

devon_research: perfect. @akshay_engineer once you have the A/B outputs give me a diff stat (mean tokens, % of responses with explicit follow-ups). I'll prepare a regression ticket and suggested rollback window if metrics exceed thresholds.

akshay_engineer: A/B run started — will post a summary in ~20m.

maria_support: I messaged the customer — told them we suspect an overzealous post-filter tied to latency mitigation and that we're investigating. Promise to update in 4 hours. They appreciated the quick response. :thumbsup:

maria_support: please keep me looped; I'll forward the A/B summary and any rollback ETA to the customer once we have it. Thanks all.
